content.title: Threshold dynamics in coastal vulnerability and adaptive governance pathways: a case study of Jiaozhou Bay social-ecological system
content.abstract: Introduction Under the background of United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 14 (Life Below Water), multi-agent collaborative governance of marine eco-economic systems faces prominent practical challenges. Coastal social-ecological vulnerability assessment and dynamic prediction are essential to support scientific marine governance. This study takes Jiaozhou Bay as the research area to explore the long-term evolutionary characteristics, driving factors and optimal governance paths of its coastal social-ecological vulnerability.
